title: Stanley Robillard inquest releases findings
subtitle: Recommendations focus on quality of care he received in hospital emergency
article: An inquest into the death of Stanley Robillard has concluded that he died accidentally of blunt force trauma to the back of the head, with alcohol as a contributing factor.

Robillard was arrested three years ago for public intoxication in Saskatoon and later found unresponsive in a police detention cell. The 46-year-old died after being transported to Royal University Hospital.

The inquest also heard testimony that Robillard had earlier been to the emergency room at St. Paul's Hospital and had checked himself out. He had not seen a doctor. The Saskatoon Health Region's head of emergency services, Dr. James Stempien, testified that the system failed Robillard.

Among the recommendations were that hours be increased at City Hospital's emergency department and in minor emergency clinics. Patients classified as 1, 2 or 3 on the Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale should have their vital signs checked more frequently. The triage process should be eliminated or bypassed when a patient is classified as CTAS 1, 2 or 3. In shift changes, briefing on the status of patients in triage should be improved.

Information sharing between police, ambulance, and hospital staff should be improved regarding the severity of injuries. The paramedic position at the detention centre should be made permanent. The brief detox unit should be expanded. Emergency departments should be staffed with more doctors during peak times.

There should be a public awareness campaign about treatment options in minor emergency clinics. Health care improvements should be audited more frequently, with measurable results and follow-up. Hospitals should have a secure ward. When a patient leaves the hospital against medical advice, there should be an audio recording of the interaction between the patient and staff, and staff signature on the release form should be mandatory.
